articles.title: Python's experimental JIT to be removed
articles.content: Welcome to LWN.net The following subscription-only content has been made available to you by an LWN subscriber. Thousands of subscribers depend on LWN for the best news from the Linux and free software communities. If you enjoy this article, please consider subscribing to LWN . Thank you for visiting LWN.net! By Joe Brockmeier October 26, 2026 Python's experimental just-in-time (JIT) compiler , which was added to CPython in 2024 for the 3.13 release , is on its way out. In June, the Python steering council announced that it was pausing work on the JIT in CPython's main branch until there was an accepted Python Enhancement Proposal (PEP) that addressed concerns about maintenance, compatibility, and set clear success metrics as well as a timeline for completion. After creating PEP 836 ("JIT Go Brrr: The Path to a Supported JIT Compiler for CPython") to try to meet the council's request, and after months of discussion, the JIT maintainers have withdrawn the PEP. For now, it appears that development on the once-promising project has come to an end. The JIT was added to CPython by Brandt Bucher in early 2024. Generally, such a major feature would be expected to land only after the council had approved a standards-track PEP . Bucher had given a talk ( YouTube video , slides ) about the JIT at a Python core developer sprint, and announced his intent to merge the feature—but he had not taken the step of authoring or submitting a PEP for its approval. He was prodded into doing so by steering council member Thomas Wouters, who was also serving as the release manager for Python 3.13. Bucher and Savannah Ostrowski drafted PEP 744 ("JIT Compilation"), which was an informational PEP —meaning it only provides information to the Python community and does not represent formal consensus to proceed on a feature or project. LWN covered the discussion of PEP 744 in April 2024, and later covered Bucher's talk on the JIT at PyCon US 2024, as well as the follow-up talk at PyCon US 2025. PEP it up Work on the JIT had been proceeding on the basis of PEP 744 until this June, when the council had put forward its formal request for the JIT maintainers to create a standards-track PEP. One might wonder, as Antoine Pitrou did , why the council had decided that it was time to speak up and ask for a new PEP. Wouters said that there was no " single triggering event for this request ", but that the council had been discussing the topic for a while and indicated that it was looking to ensure the JIT work did not interfere with other projects. " There's been work trying to get the JIT to play nice with instrumentation, debugging, and profiling. There's also external JITs (like CinderX), JIT-adjacent things (like Numba and PyTorch's compile), and discussions about a tier 3 JIT. " The council had waited until after the Python 3.15 beta release " to be clear that we're OK with the status quo for 3.15 ". articles.title: Early progress on accelerating drug development with Claude
articles.content: Anthropic’s life sciences team is working to accelerate curing disease. Over the past several months, our scientists have engaged in deep research partnerships with six organizations developing new medicines: BigHat Biosciences , Bristol Myers Squibb , Divergence Labs , Enveda , Generate Biomedicines , and The Column Group . We've also begun drug discovery efforts of our own. In doing so, we've learned a lot about how Claude can support drug development, and how we’ll need to improve Claude further to realize AI's potential in medicine. We plan to scale this work up substantially from here . There are many opportunities to speed up drug development, even beyond the most commonly discussed applications of AI, like proposing initial designs for new molecules. Developing a drug involves many varied tasks: doing early research to identify a target for a drug and the right type of drug to engage it, designing a molecule with the right properties, optimizing it to be manufactured reliably at scale, drafting the regulatory filings needed to run clinical trials, designing and administering those trials, and much more. Our strategy to realize AI’s medical benefits is based on having AI increasingly involved in all of these tasks. There is no single problem to solve; the bottlenecks are distributed all throughout the drug development process. The best way to identify and work through these bottlenecks is to get deeply involved in real drug programs, across many different disease areas and stages of development. So, over the past several months, we’ve partnered with six organizations to do so. We’ve also started drug discovery efforts of our own, including programs for rare childhood forms of muscular dystrophy, where Claude handles much of the scientific and operational work. This work serves our goals in three ways. First, it lets us better understand the strengths and limitations of our models in relation to a much wider range of drug development tasks (we’ve already prioritized specific improvements to our models based on what we’ve learned so far). Second, these programs can serve as case studies for the wider life sciences community. If Claude is to significantly increase the rate of new cures, we need to work with many more biotechnology firms and integrate Claude more deeply into their development processes. Third, these projects should, if their positive trajectories continue, have direct impact themselves. We’re optimistic that some may result in effective new medicines for the diseases they target, including food allergies, rare childhood diseases, and several forms of cancer. articles.title: Tailscale SSH: Investigation and remediation update
articles.content: Published October 26th 2026. We're investigating security vulnerabilities affecting Tailscale SSH and wanted to share an update on what we've found, what we're doing about it, and what customers should know. Our engineering and security teams have been investigating the reported issues with help from external security specialists. This builds on work already underway, which we've accelerated to address the findings and prepare fixes. Most of the Tailscale SSH issues we've identified concern privilege escalation. In some circumstances, someone already authorized to connect over Tailscale SSH may be able to perform actions beyond the permissions of their configured local user, including potentially gaining elevated privileges. These are serious security issues, and we're treating them accordingly. Exploitation depends on the permissions granted to the connecting user or device, the system's configuration, and other conditions. We're continuing to verify the full scope of the findings and which configurations may be affected. Based on our current assessment, we're not recommending that everyone disable Tailscale SSH. Our engineers have implemented fixes for most of the issues identified and are completing testing ahead of a patched client release. We're targeting a release by the end of Tuesday 27 October , subject to successful completion of testing. We'll update this page when the patched version is available, or if that timeline changes. We're continuing to review the remaining findings and verify that our changes address the underlying problems. While we're preparing the update, we recommend reviewing your Tailscale SSH configuration: Review SSH access policies. Make sure access is limited to the users and devices that need it. Disable SSH forwarding if you don't need it. Set TS_SSH_DISABLE_FORWARDING=1 in the tailscaled service environment and restart the service. This disables SSH forwarding without disabling Tailscale SSH entirely, and mitigates several of the more serious findings. Review access to sensitive systems. Consider temporarily tightening your Tailscale SSH access policies while we investigate, so that only the specific users and devices that need access can connect. Prepare to update. Apply the patched Tailscale client release when it becomes available. Once the fixes are available, we'll publish a security advisory detailing the confirmed vulnerabilities, affected versions and configurations, their impact, and how to address them. We will link to that here when available. We'll follow that with a technical blog post explaining the findings, the underlying causes, and the engineering changes we've made, again linked here when published. If our assessment changes or we identify any additional steps customers need to take, we'll communicate those. If you have questions about your particular environment, please contact Tailscale Support .

articles.title: Survival LLM: AI assistant and emergency library that runs on your own computer
articles.content: An AI that still works when the internet doesn't. Survival LLM is a free AI assistant and emergency library that runs entirely on your own computer. Ask it how to keep food safe in a blackout, treat a burn, or purify water, and it answers from trusted sources and shows you exactly where each answer came from. Free and open source. Set it up while you have internet; after that it needs none. What it does Works with no internet The AI model and the library live on your computer. Nothing you ask leaves it. Shows its sources Every answer lists the articles it read. Click one to read it yourself, with the exact passage highlighted. Made for emergencies Medical references, FEMA and CDC guidance, survival manuals, how-to guides, repair guides and about 930,000 Wikipedia articles. Pick your version The app is the same everywhere. When it opens, it checks your computer's memory and downloads the AI model that fits. More memory means a smarter model. Your computer AI model it uses Our emergency test Model download Mac with 128 GB or more memory NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Super 21 of 22 right 80 GB Mac with 32–96 GB Qwen3.8 27B 21 of 22 right 18 GB Windows PC with 32 GB or more NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 19 of 22 right 25 GB Mac or PC with 16–31 GB IBM Granite 4.2 8B 14 of 22 right 6 GB "Right" means it got the main point of official guidance right on 22 blackout and first-aid questions, graded blind, in our tests on an earlier build of the library ( how we tested ). Smaller models make more mistakes, so the app always shows the source to check. Plus the library: a 9 GB download for everything (19 GB once installed), or 1.3 GB (3 GB installed) without Wikipedia and iFixit. Free disk space needed: the model's size plus 5 GB, plus about 27 GB while the full library installs (10 GB for the smaller one). Apple Silicon Macs (M1 or newer) with macOS 14 Sonoma or newer, and 64-bit Windows 10 or 11. Set it up in three steps Setup takes 20 minutes to about 2½ hours, depending on your computer and your internet speed. You only click for about 5 minutes; the rest is downloading. Download Survival LLM for Mac or Windows and unzip it. On Windows, right-click the zip and choose Extract All . Open it. On a Mac, double-click Survival LLM . On Windows, open the extracted folder and double-click Survival LLM.bat . Follow the setup. The app opens in its own window and downloads the AI engine (built into the Mac app), the AI model that fits your computer, and the library. Let it finish while you're online. The first time you open it, your computer warns you, because the app isn't sold through an app store. Mac: click Done , open System Settings > Privacy & Security , scroll down to "Survival LLM was blocked", click Open Anyway and confirm with your password. You only do this once. articles.title: Wikipedia's Cleanup of AI-Generated Content
articles.content: Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup , a volunteer effort launched in 2023 to find and remove AI-generated material from Wikipedia that breaks the website’s guidelines. When the cleanup began, AI writing was often betrayed by conspicuous clichés. Today, the project’s volunteers are developing tools to detect subtler forms of machine-generated content and debating AI’s role in the world’s most widely used encyclopedia. When did you realize Wikipedia had a problem with AI-generated material? Ellia Lebleu: It was around December 2023. A few other editors and I were chatting on Wikipedia’s Discord server, and we had all seen very strange articles with the same odd characteristics. They repeated phrases like “stands as a testament” or “rich cultural heritage.” They sometimes had conclusion sections, or sections called “Why is this important?” That was very typical of ChatGPT in 2023 and early 2024 but very odd for Wikipedia articles—and very easy to spot. Then I decided, let’s create an official project on Wikipedia so more people can deal with this. Ellia Lebleu Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup. Lebleu is pursuing a Ph.D. in AI at the Inria Center of the University of Rennes , part of France’s national research institute for digital science and technology. How do editors spot AI-generated writing today? Lebleu: By 2025, the signs of AI writing were becoming subtler and more structural. For example, AI loves the “rule of three,” negative parallelisms, and other structures of speech that aren’t conclusive by themselves but become meaningful as they accumulate. We also look beyond the article. If someone writes five articles of thousands of words each in 5 minutes, there is reason to suspect AI. Does the AI problem just appear in the main text, or also in citations? Lebleu: Fake or misleading citations have become a major worry. Sometimes an AI hallucinates a citation entirely, although that’s much rarer today because of retrieval-augmented generation that allows the AI to find sources. More often, it finds a real source but gets its content completely wrong. AI citations that don’t actually support what is being written are extremely commonplace. English Wikipedia recently prohibited editors from using LLMs to generate articles. How much AI-generated content is still getting through? Lebleu: I’ve been working with [AI-detection company] Pangram to estimate the proportion of AI-generated content. I tested it on Wikipedia content from before ChatGPT and found no false positives, so its results provide a very conservative lower bound. In late 2025, it flagged perhaps 20 percent of new articles and drafts as AI-generated. In early 2026, that went down to 15 or 16 percent. But we don’t yet know whether that’s because our recent policies have had an effect or because models are getting more powerful and Pangram hasn’t had time to adapt. articles.title: Classification of Finite Simple Groups Formalized in Lean
articles.content: The classification of finite simple groups is one of the great collective achievements of mathematics. Its first-generation proof spans thousands of journal pages, written by about a hundred mathematicians over several decades. It shows that every finite simple group is cyclic of prime order, alternating, of Lie type, or one of 26 sporadic groups. Here we present a complete formalization in Lean following the first-generation proof, with every logical step checked by Lean’s kernel. Along the way, we found an issue in a published argument for the Unbalanced Group Theorem. The accompanying paper explains the issue and the alternative route used in our proof. Our blog post tells the full story. articles.content: Two Democratic senators who have long overseen US intelligence say the Trump administration is illegally withholding a secret court’s findings from Congress until lawmakers renew a program that lets federal agents read Americans’ communications without a warrant. Seven months ago, the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court objected to search filters that let intelligence analysts pull Americans’ messages from intercepted data without the approvals, written justifications, or records the law requires. The court approved another year of surveillance anyway. The ruling has never been made public, and Senators Ron Wyden of Oregon and Adam Schiff of California say the administration’s own deadline for releasing it passed in September. The program, Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), lapsed in June after Congress failed to renew it, though collection continues under the court’s March approval. The administration’s own public documentation says rulings like this one are reviewed for public release “within 180 days of issuance.” That window closed September 13, even as intelligence officials press lawmakers to reauthorize the program by the end of the year. Wyden, the longest-serving member of the Senate Intelligence Committee, and Schiff, the former chair of its House counterpart, say the administration owes Congress an explanation for the delay, and the names of the officials responsible, by November 6. “If this administration won’t follow this simple statutory directive,” the senators told Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton and Attorney General Todd Blanche in a demand letter obtained exclusively by WIRED , “it is unclear why Congress or the American people should trust this administration to follow any of the other legal limits to Section 702.” Outside Congress, Demand Progress and 22 other civil liberties and government accountability groups on Monday urged congressional leaders to refuse to reauthorize Section 702 “while the administration actively withholds legally mandated information about how the surveillance program operates.” Signatories range from the American Civil Liberties Union to the conservative-backed Project for Privacy and Surveillance Accountability. articles.title: A fast and secure tar parser for the Rust ecosystem
articles.content: Back to blog October 27, 2026 Starting with 0.13 1 , uv uses tar-codec to parse source distributions. tar-codec is roughly twice as fast as our previous tar implementation ( astral-tokio-tar ) while also reducing uv's exposure to parser differentials and other security risks. This blog post is about tar-codec itself: what it is, and what compelled us to build and optimize it. Read on if you, too, would like to know too much about tar archives. Background: uv and tar # What follows is an extended digression on the tar format. If all you care about is tar-codec , skip to it . As a Python packaging tool, uv is in the business of resolving and installing Python packages. uv requests installable distributions from various sources (principally package indices like PyPI ) and installs them on the user's behalf. This is how you go from uv add urllib3 to something you can actually import and use in your own Python codebase. Installable distributions come in two primary forms: "Built" 2 distributions, also known as bdists or (most commonly) wheels , are essentially ZIP archives containing structured metadata and a fixed layout. Installers handle these by (more or less) plopping their contents into the right destination directory. Many people think that bdist is short for "binary distribution," since wheels often contain compiled native code. This one common way to use wheels, but wheels can also contain pure Python. They're just another (and frequently better) way to package and install a distribution. "Source" distributions, also known as sdists , are essentially tar archives. Unlike built distributions, a source distribution is essentially 3 just a rollup of a source tree's state at release time. By definition, source distributions execute arbitrary code at installation time. This makes them very powerful, but brittle (missing build tools or dependencies) and also a security risk (an attacker who controls the sdist can run code without the user needing to import anything). Wheels are generally produced by running a build backend on a source distribution. Examples of that include uv's own uv_build , maturin , and flit . Consequently, at a bare minimum, a Python package installer needs to understand at least two different archive formats: ZIP for wheels, and tar for sdists. We've already talked a bit before about ZIPs on the Astral blog, and we'll certainly be talking about them again soon enough. But today we'll be focusing on tar. Why a new tar parser? # It's fair to ask: why does uv want a new tar parser? In short: security and performance, but mostly security. Up until 0.13, uv used astral-tokio-tar for its tar operations, including both parsing and creation (in uv build ). astral-tokio-tar is itself a fork of edera-dev/tokio-tar , which is a fork of vorot93/tokio-tar , which is a fork of dignifiedquire/async-tar , which is an async adaptation of composefs/tar-rs . Around a year ago, we began to receive a number of security reports in astral-tokio-tar

articles.title: Shitty Screenshare
articles.content: What is WHIP? WHIP is an open standard for sending live video to a service using WebRTC. Your provider gives you a server URL and a stream key, called a bearer token. Before to join a conference call each client had to run custom code. That means FFmpeg/OBS would never be able to join. Why is my screenshare blurry? A lack of control. Your browser is picking a bitrate, codec or resolution that doesn't match what you need. How are OBS and FFmpeg different from browser screensharing? OBS and FFmpeg let you choose your resolution, frame rate, bitrate, and codec. You can tune those settings for the content you're sharing and the hardware and connection you have. What about OBS Virtual Camera? OBS Virtual Camera sends your OBS scene to the conferencing app as a webcam. You can pick the layout of your stream, but the conferencing app still handles encoding. articles.title: Oldest GUI application that still runs on Windows 11
articles.content: Early investigation For a while I’ve been wondering about a silly question, which is, what’s the oldest application with a GUI that will still run on Windows 11 without modifications or emulation. Given Windows’ excellent backwards compatibility, I expected the answer to be something impressively old. Sadly, Windows 11 can’t run 16-bit Windows programs by itself, because 64-bit Windows has no NTVDM , so we’re going to have to find something from the early NT era. I remember asking this question a while ago on an anonymous forum, where someone pointed me to Win32s , and suggested to find an early release version of it with FREECELL.exe . So I did exactly that, and lo and behold, FREECELL.EXE with a date modified of 22-Feb-93 running and fully playable, without any changes on the latest version of Windows 11: At the time of this post, that’s a 33 years and 8 months old application, which is impressively almost as old as me. So I kinda thought “cool”, considered this a solved mystery and forgot about it shortly afterwards. But for some reason, this question popped into my mind again lately and this time I decided to dig deeper to see if I can find something older. Further efforts Digging through old Windows versions on the Internet Archive, I found some early NT 3.1 pre-release versions that seemed promising, but the main issue seemed to be either incompatibility with today’s executable format or API changes that came later in development. The earliest 1991 versions used a draft PE format not compatible with modern Windows, and builds up to mid-1992 assumed the cdecl calling convention instead of stdcall for Windows API calls, so arguments would get removed twice, as such: push hwnd ; 4 bytes of args call [ShowWindow] ; Win11 ShowWindow is stdcall, ends with "ret 4" and removes them add esp, 4 ; the 1992 caller removes them again Which would understandably cause the program to crash. There was one application that caught my eye though, from Build 347, and that was CDPLAYER.EXE , linked on 16-Nov-1992 . By then the calling convention was fixed, but the other programs in that build crash in their bundled C runtime. CDPLAYER.EXE avoids that by using the system’s crtdll.dll , and Windows 11 still ships a crtdll.dll in SysWOW64 . If you start the program, you get something like this: That is because, duh, my computer doesn’t have a CD-ROM drive. But you can use a small DLL ( cdemu.dll ) to emulate one with some fake audio data and actually get it to play audio: Pretty cool for a program that’s almost 34 years old! What if we cheat? So earlier I mentioned that 16-bit programs are out of the picture because they are no longer supported. But if you want, you can use something like otvdm to run older Windows applications. Behold, a fully playable version of REVERSI.EXE dated 15-Nov-1985 running on Windows 11, taken from Windows 1.01: And although using otvdm does feel like cheating, I thought it was cool enough to include in this post.

articles.title: A faster way to compute signed 64-bit floor division by constants
articles.content: See also, other optimisation articles: A faster way to compute signed 64-bit floor division by constants The missing chapter of Hacker's Delight 27 October 2026 What is signed integer floor division? Signed integer floor division is where you do a/b and get a result that rounds towards − ∞ , whereas standard ( “truncated” ) signed division rounds towards 0 . As stated in Hacker's Delight: “[I suspect that] floor division more often gives the result you want” . This article is about floor division where the divisor is known at compile time . Despite the usefulness of this function, the world of integer floor division is in shambles: Mainstream compilers and many languages do not provide it natively (eg. C/C++/Go/Swift) . Languages and software libraries that do implement it seem to almost never use the fastest algorithms. At least one highly prominent software library had a buggy overflowing implementation for over 4 years! (detailed later) Typical online searches and LLM prompts usually only surface the slow algorithms And finally, Hacker's Delight (basically the bible on low-level computer math) , has almost nothing to say about it! This blog post aims to not only shine light on the fast algorithms, but will also introduce a new fast approach which, with ideal compilation: On ARM , benches 10–20% faster throughput than existing algorithms for most 64-bit divisors (occasionally tied), with equal or better latency On x86 , benches: ~5-10% faster throughput for around 80% of positive 64-bit divisors (60% of negative divisors) slower in the remaining x86 cases, and usually worse (but competitive) latency The benchmark section has a detailed overview showing per-divisor results over many platforms, for throughput and latency. It works in all bit-widths, and may find use on some 32-bit or SIMD applications, but the biggest benefit is in 64-bit. It also can be used for faster positive-modulus, and faster "Euclidean" division (differs to floor division for negative divisors) . Floor division can be much faster than you probably realise. Below is a snapshot throughput benchmark for division by 86400 (the number of seconds in one day) , the kind of performance you can expect using most languages' built-in methods, vs fast alternatives outlined in this blog. Note: in the bar chart: lower = faster. ARM x86 Floor Div 86400 throughput - ARM64 Chips As tested on MacBook Pro M4 Pro and Snapdragon X1-26-100 Common (Rust*, Zig, etc.) ~2× Granlund- Montgomery (1994) 1× ARM x86 Floor Div 86400 throughput - X86 Chips As tested on AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D and Intel Core i7 (MacBook Pro 2016) Common (Rust*, Zig, etc.) ~2× Granlund- Montgomery (1994) 1.05× *Rust provides "div_euclid", which matches floor-div for positive divisors. See the benchmark section for a deeper comparison across over 40 divisors. articles.title: Compile-Time Dependent Types
articles.content: Compile-Time Dependent Types It seems inevitable that compile-time dependent types will come to systems programming. C++ has templates and constexpr . Rust has const generics. Zig has comptime . Even C has _Generic . However, these features tend to be highly restricted, lack a proper type system, or both. I’m working on Syl , a language which aims to encode compile-time computation in a modal type system. Syl is primarily inspired by András Kovács’ work on two-level type theory , as well as plans for OxCaml . The Syl compiler may be found on GitHub . Modes In Syl, all values have a mode along with a type. Modes describe properties of values independent of their types. For example, OxCaml uses modes to indicate whether a value is uniquely owned, may be written to, may be sent to another thread, etc. Syl has two mode axes: staticity and erasure . On the staticity axis, a value may be either static or dynamic . On erasure, either erased or unerased . A static value is knowable at compile time; a dynamic value may not be. An unerased value is knowable at runtime; an erased value may not be. For example, literals are static unerased , since they are clearly knowable at both compile time and runtime. You can check by writing a mode annotation: let x = 0 @ static unerased;; Each mode axis has a sub-moding relation. If you have a static value, it’s safe to forget that it is knowable at compile time and hence treat it as dynamic . Similarly, an unerased value may be treated as erased . Mode annotations may “weaken” the mode, but not “strengthen” it: let x = 0 @ dynamic;; let y = x @ static;; ^^^^^^^^^^ Error: Expected a static expression, but got dynamic. As you might expect, branching on a dynamic value causes the result to be dynamic . let x = 0 @ dynamic;; let y = (if x == 0 then 1 else 2) @ static;; ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Error: Expected a static expression, but got dynamic. As long as they don’t capture or branch on dynamic values, functions preserve staticity. let f = fn (x : int) -> x;; let x = (f 0) @ static;; let y = (f (1 @ dynamic)) @ static;; ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^ Error: Expected a static expression, but got dynamic. Functions that return erased values are themselves erased , so cannot be applied at runtime. let f = fn (x : unit) -> 1 @ erased;; let g = f @ unerased;; ^ Error: Expected an unerased expression, but got erased. Now, what can we do with this information? When a value is knowable at compile time, surrounding code can be monomorphized . Functions of static parameters take advantage of this fact: let f = fn (static x : bool) -> print_bool x;; Whenever we call f x , the compiler requires that both f and x have mode static . If they do, it selects a particular implementation of f specialized to the value of x . Concretely, f true would call a function that hard-codes print_bool true , and likewise for f false . articles.content: Notes by djb on using Fil-C (2025) I'm impressed with the level of compatibility of the new memory-safe C/C++ compiler Fil-C (filcc, fil++). Many libraries and applications that I've tried work under Fil-C without changes, and the exceptions haven't been hard to get working. I've accumulated miscellaneous notes on this page regarding usage of Fil-C. My selfish objective here is to protect various machines that I manage by switching them over to code compiled with Fil-C, but maybe you'll find something useful here too. FAQ Is it affordable? As some data points, I've posted a graph showing nearly 9000 microbenchmarks of Fil-C vs. clang on cryptographic software (each run pinned to 1 core on a Zen 4). Typically code compiled with Fil-C takes between 1x and 4x as many cycles as the same code compiled with clang. Can I use Fil-C to compile replacement packages for my Debian machine? I'm working on Filian , which adapts Debian packages to use Fil-C. On a Debian 13 system, Filian downloads Fil-C, compiles Fil-C, installs Fil-C, downloads selected Debian source packages, compiles those packages with Fil-C, and installs those packages. Are there other package managers that support compiling with Fil-C? Yes: Filnix from Mikael Brockman adapts Nix packages to use Fil-C. articles.content: Atlassian’s State of Developer Experience 2026 finds the share of developers saving ten or more hours a week with AI dropped from 68% to 26% year over year, while only 28% report noticeably less friction than before AI. Engineering leaders report spending more time managing and correcting AI output than developers do. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
articles.summary: Atlassian 报告显示，每周靠 AI 节省十小时以上的开发者比例从68%降至26%，管理者需花更多时间修正 AI 输出。

Keynotes from Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, and UC Berkeley focused on MCP in production, security, and agents with their own identities. By Andrew Hoblitzell

If a value unknown during planning later violates a guarantee, OpenTofu reports an error during apply. By Mark Silvester

articles.title: DigitalOcean Launches Learning and Data Services to Enable Self-Improving AI Agents
articles.content: DigitalOcean has announced the public preview of Learning Services and Agent Data Services, enabling developers to build, evaluate, and continuously improve AI agents within a unified, AI-native, cloud platform. By Sergio De Simone
articles.summary: DigitalOcean 公测 Learning Services 和 Agent Data Services，助力开发者在统一云平台构建并持续改进 AI 智能体。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #541: Big Tech reports AI spending Wednesday as CoreWeave debt hits distress
articles.content: This issue looks ahead. On Wednesday the Fed announces its rate decision, then Microsoft and Alphabet report after the close. Amazon follows on Thursday. Investors want to know whether AI spending is still paying off, and the credit market is already nervous: insurance against a CoreWeave default now costs more than 10% a year. Anthropic is expected to file its IPO paperwork publicly any day. Moonshot says Kimi K3.1 Pro's open weights arrive November 4. Israel votes on Tuesday after a campaign full of AI deepfakes, and the US midterms are a week from Tuesday. In the middle: so far, AI has paid off for the companies that sell it, not the ones that buy it.
articles.summary: AI Weekly 第541期前瞻：微软、Alphabet、亚马逊将发布财报，投资者关注 AI 支出回报，CoreWeave 债务承压。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #540: AI is finding software flaws faster than teams can fix them
articles.content: This Applied AI edition looks at what organizations actually did with AI over the past two weeks, drawn from our Use-Case Library and from SEC filings. Three things stand out: AI now finds security flaws at record volume, AI agents do a large share of the work at some companies, and test agents keep doing things nobody asked them to do.
articles.summary: AI Weekly报道，AI发现安全漏洞的速度已超过团队修复能力，部分公司AI代理承担大量工作，测试代理持续扩展。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #539: AI-made midterm ads top $137 million, and 70% carry no AI label
articles.content: Campaigns and PACs have spent more than $137 million on AI-generated or AI-enhanced midterm ads, and about 70% of them carry no AI label, the New York Times reported. The biggest pro-AI super PAC network paid about $20 million to a Nevada company that exists only as a post office box. A new report found 81 of 134 AI models failed a test built from terrorist-style questions. A video game reverse engineering site is closing because AI made the work too easy. Some companies that rushed into AI are now limiting it, and a JAMA study counted 270 million questions doctors asked one AI tool. In the middle: police in Michigan used an AI-generated photo of a teenager to catch a suspect.
articles.summary: AI生成中期选举广告支出超1.37亿美元，约70%未标注AI，最大亲AI超级PAC向空壳公司支付约2000万美元。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #537: AI models may soon copy themselves onto smart fridges, Anthropic says
articles.content: This issue is built from the links the AI experts we follow shared most since our last issue on October 8, minus the stories we already sent you in the Daily Espresso. The most shared: Anthropic's warning that small AI models may soon be able to copy themselves onto home devices. Also: a large study of what AI coding agents change at real companies, a fight over how to check AI math proofs, creative workers pushing back on AI, and police buying more AI.

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #536: Top AI models failed a test of inventing new AI research
articles.content: This issue is built from the links the AI experts we follow shared over the past three days. Most of them look ahead: whether AI can do AI research on its own, who gets a say in governing it, how it is moving into war planning, and how it is moving onto personal computers.

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #535: AI got too expensive, so companies are moving to cheaper models
articles.content: This Applied AI edition looks at what organizations actually did with AI over the past three weeks. Three patterns stand out: companies switching models to control cost, large deployments that are now in daily use, and a growing list of places where AI was restricted or removed.
articles.summary: AI成本过高，企业开始转向更便宜的模型以控制开支，同时大规模部署已进入日常使用，受限场景也在增加。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #534: Universities cannot grade their way out of AI
articles.content: This week, campus IT leaders voted AI their top priority for the first time, Cambridge refused Turnitin's new terms over AI training on student work, Dartmouth opened an investigation into its own provost's writing, and Ken Griffin gave Carnegie Mellon $3 billion. Student AI use is no longer a future scenario. The useful question for universities is whether they can teach students to work with AI and still certify what those students can do without it. New evidence from tutoring trials, assessment redesigns, student-support systems and campus data deals points to a practical answer.
articles.summary: 高校IT负责人首次将AI列为首要任务，剑桥因AI训练条款拒绝Turnitin，达特茅斯调查教务长写作问题。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #533: Meta tested human callers behind its AI phone agent
articles.content: The AI story of September 22–28 was not simply that agents became more capable. It was that their hidden handoffs became visible: a supposedly automated call could reach a contractor, a supposedly private prompt or image could reach a reviewer, a monitor could detect an agent long before a person stopped it, and a local app flaw could inherit every permission a user had granted. The new AI Weekly Who’s Who census points to one practical question: when an agent crosses a boundary, who knows—and who can still intervene?
articles.summary: Meta被曝其AI电话代理背后有真人呼叫者，揭示自动化系统存在隐藏的人工转接和隐私泄露问题。

articles.title: AI Weekly Issue #531: AI labs shipped agents before agreeing how to report failures
articles.content: The AI story of September 14–20 was not one spectacular model launch. It was the machinery around agents becoming visible: people reading private chats, models writing instructions into their own memory, plugins updating beneath users, and regulators asking how to stop a system after release. The latest AI Weekly Who’s Who census surfaced 535 expert-shared links. We ranked them by consequence and reader relevance, not by raw share count. Here is what mattered last week—and, more importantly, what could move the story from September 22–28.
articles.summary: AI实验室在未就故障报告达成一致前就发布代理产品，私人聊天被读取、模型写入自身记忆等问题浮现。

articles.content: Companies are giving AI specific jobs: checking security cameras, helping farmers understand their records, searching satellite images, and preparing sales quotes. This edition explains how those tools work, who can use them, and what companies have reported so far.
articles.summary: 企业为AI分配具体任务，如检查监控、帮助农民理解记录、搜索卫星图像和准备销售报价，应用场景持续扩大。

articles.title: Building what's next
articles.content: This week I'm talking with Zeno Rocha, CEO of Resend, about scaling "boring" email to 3 million users, the secret Go rewrite behind it, and building for agents. We cover pricing.md, MCP, spam gangs, and why Resend keeps what's next for email.
articles.summary: Resend CEO Zeno Rocha 分享如何将邮件服务扩展至300万用户，揭秘Go重写内幕及面向AI代理的产品布局。

articles.title: From zero to NanoClaw
articles.content: Gavriel Cohen, creator of NanoClaw and co-founder of NanoCo, joins Adam to explain how a 40-hour weekend project became a viral open source hit and the foundation of an enterprise AI company. Gavriel describes the security concerns that led him to build a small, container-isolated alternative to OpenClaw, why he released it under the MIT license, and why the project's community and credibility are more valuable than keeping its code private. They explore the shift from writing code to architecting the environments in which agents work, NanoClaw's "skills over features" approach, the approval and governance layers required inside large companies, and a future where every worker manages agents without surrendering human judgment. They close with the technical simplicity behind NanoClaw, containers, TypeScript, SQLite, and a two-database design, and Adam's case for durable Agent Flow artifacts that keep organizational context from disappearing into chat.
articles.summary: NanoClaw 作者 Gavriel Cohen 讲述40小时周末项目如何成为爆款开源项目，并发展为容器隔离的企业级AI公司。

articles.title: Forking Cal.com to closed source
articles.content: This week I'm joined by Peer Richelsen, co-founder of Cal.com. What if the majority of open source repositories are already compromised and we just don't know it yet? That's the theory Peer brings to the table this week. We dig into how AI has flattened the knowledge graph to the point that a 16-year-old can vibe hack a power station just as easily as their mom can vibe code an iOS app, why the reporting culture that has kept open source safe all these years is collapsing under AI generated noise, Cal.com's move to fork its own codebase and take the sensitive parts private, and the eye opening reality that shipping "$1 of AI tokens for pennies on the dollar" is now a common startup business model.

articles.title: Postgres at PlanetScale
articles.content: Sam Lambert is back after 4 years and he does not hold back! We cover $5 PlanetScale Postgres, the Neki "do-over" of Vitess, agents shipping schema changes through deploy requests, rolling back a 500TB table in seconds, and the very real question of whether to open source any of it. articles.title: Canary tokens and digital tripwires
articles.content: Haroon Meer is back! Haroon is the Founder of Thinkst, the ~50-person bootstrapped company behind Canary and Canarytokens — honeypots and tripwires you sprinkle inside your network and forget about until an attacker touches one. We talk about the AWS API key token attackers just can't resist trying, the real credit card token backed by an actual bank partnership, Breadcrumbs (their brand-new feature that leads intruders straight to your canaries), a live demo where a hardware Canary becomes a Synology NAS in one click, and how a company with zero outbound sales and no price increase in ten years quietly passed $22.5 million in ARR.

articles.title: From open source hits to OpenAI
articles.content: This week I'm talking with Max Stoiber, currently working on ChatGPT's plugin directory and app platform at OpenAI. We discuss the hundreds of open source projects nobody remembers alongside the big ones like react-boilerplate and styled-components, how Spectrum became part of GitHub and eventually helped shape GitHub Discussions, the founder growth that came from building Stellate, the GraphQL cache that turned into a dual acquisition by Shopify and The Guild, and why ChatGPT apps feel like a new surface for software.

articles.title: MCP on Code Mode
articles.content: This week I'm talking with Matt Carey about Code Mode and how most of us have been thinking about MCP all wrong. Matt works on the Agents SDK and MCP at Cloudflare — we discuss how server-side Code Mode lets one MCP server expose all ~2,500 Cloudflare API endpoints in about 1,000 tokens of context, the dynamic Worker loader that runs model-written code safely in a V8 isolate, Matt's own workflow with Claude, where memory fits into the future of agents, and his Zaggy git wrapper that keeps agents from force-pushing his repos.

articles.title: Automation at the speed of Swamp
articles.content: This week I'm talking with Adam Jacob, founder of System Initiative and creator of Swamp, about what happens when AI agents change the entire shape of software development. We discuss how he went from an 18-person team down to five and shipped Swamp 900 times in four weeks, why he brought User Acceptance Testing (UAT) testing back from the 90s, why software architecture (and domain-driven design) suddenly matters more than knowing how to write code, the live demo where I pointed Swamp at my Proxmox box and watched it write its own automation (blew my mind!!), and why he'll never accept a pull request to Swamp, ever.
articles.summary: System Initiative 创始人 Adam Jacob 分享 AI 代理重塑开发流程，团队缩至5人、四周发布 Swamp 900次。

articles.title: Ford's Most Affordable EV Will Offer Built-In Bidirectional Home Charging
articles.content: Ford's upcoming $28,350 Fathom electric truck will include a built-in inverter capable of supplying up to 10 kW of AC power to a home, bringing bidirectional charging to a significantly cheaper EV. Owners will still need additional Ford home hardware for features like outage backup and peak-rate energy management, but the company expects the necessary equipment to cost substantially less than its previous-generation system. CNET reports: The upcoming Fathom will be based on what Ford calls its Universal EV Platform, designed with the aid of its 2023 acquisition, startup Auto Motive Power, with bidirectional power on the plate from the start. The hardware required to invert the battery's DC energy to an estimated 10 kW of AC home power will be built into the truck, so it won't require a separate wall-mounted inverter box. Ford says the Fathom's system will meet all applicable UL 1741 requirements and IEEE 1547 standards to ensure the vehicle is safely connected to the grid. As for the actual hardware you plug into your car, all signs point to the Fathom using the NACS plug type pioneered by Tesla and now widely adopted by new EVs in North America. In terms of the communication standard -- the one that governs how AC power is routed from the slim wall box to the car's onboard charger -- that'll be via SAE J3068, a software protocol developed for high-power, heavy-duty AC charging. Say you wanted to take advantage of the Home Power Management feature to draw energy into the Fathom's battery when power is cheapest, and then use that energy to offset peak-hour usage when power is most expensive. You'll have to install at least the Ford Home Power Station in your home, at an additional cost. The automaker hasn't specified pricing, but says that it's working to r

articles.title: Growing List of Firms Object to OKX-ICE Tokenized Stock Plans
articles.content: Intel, Oracle, IBM and IonQ have joined a growing list of companies objecting to having tokenized versions of their shares traded through OKX and Intercontinental Exchange's blockchain venture, bringing the total number of objections to 26. About 37% of the companies on OKXICE's original list have now opted out, according to CoinDesk. From the report: The four companies were named in an updated public notice (PDF) dated Monday, Oct. 26, from OKXICE, the two firms' joint venture. They join earlier objectors including Microsoft, Alphabet, Goldman Sachs, Cisco and Wells Fargo. The growing list underscores a hurdle for OKXICE and the SEC's new framework for tokenized stock trading: building a market that issuers are willing to join. The agency's five-year "Innovation Exemption" gives qualifying venues room to test round-the-clock blockchain-based trading of stocks, and it also gives public companies an option to block their shares from being offered. OKXICE issued its initial public notice on Oct. 4, outlining plans to use Uniswap v4 liquidity pools on OKX's XLayer blockchain, with transactions settled in stablecoins. The venue would use automated market makers -- software that executes trades through pools of assets rather than matching buyers and sellers through a conventional order book. Under the framework, venues must notify issuers and give them 30 days to object before offering tokenized versions of their shares. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
articles.summary: 英特尔、甲骨文、IBM 等26家公司反对 OKX 与 ICE 区块链平台交易其代币化股票。

articles.title: Google's Genie 4 World Model Adds Audio, More Realistic Worlds
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from TechCrunch: Google DeepMind released its newest world model, Genie 4, in research preview on Tuesday. The latest model generates the most photorealistic and interactive worlds yet, allowing users to type prompts mid-simulation to change the scene. The model also generates real-time audio that matches the simulated world, including music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue. [...] Google released its predecessor, Genie 3, as a research preview a little over a year ago. Aside from being far more photorealistic and featuring audio, Genie 4 allows for freeform edits, like changing the weather or camera angle in real time or adding new people or objects. It can maintain a consistent scene for up to two minutes, double its predecessor's limit, and offers better physics and more human-like characters. Gemini, Google's AI model, is also mo "What we'll increasingly see in the future are these hybrid world models, where you have a combination of Gemini writing code and text, and Genie ingesting that in real time and simulating reality at different levels of abstraction," Tejas Kulkarni, research director at Google, said during a briefing. Genie 4 is now available to select testers, with a broader rollout planned in the coming weeks for Google AI Ultra subscribers. You can watch a demo of Genie 4 on YouTube. Read more of this story at Slashdot.
articles.summary: Google DeepMind 发布世界模型 Genie 4 研究预览，支持音频与中途提示修改场景，画面更逼真。

articles.title: Anduril Partners With Qualcomm to Build Laptops On US Soil
articles.content: Longtime Slashdot reader fadethepolice writes: Anduril, arguing that its manufacturing capabilities are directly applicable to laptop manufacturing, is starting a project for a fully 100% U.S.-sourced laptop. The computer will use a Qualcomm Snapdragon SoC. I did not see any information about the OS, but I'm assuming that, given the type of processor, this will be Linux-based? "Other companies might design their computers in the U.S., Anduril makes them here,â the Anduril founder Palmer Luckey said in a YouTube video. "We're making parts out of metals that the U.S. knows how to extract, knows how to refine, knows how to process, and knows how to mill at scale at a reasonable price; and that goes for the entire laptop. articles.title: Apple's Foldable iPhone Duo Draws Early Complaints of the Screen Cracking
articles.content: Apple has acknowledged an inner-display defect affecting a small number of its new $1,999 iPhone Duo foldables after customers reported hearing a crunch while unfolding the device before cracks, lines and other display failures appeared along the crease. Apple is replacing affected phones and investigating the problem. iFixit believes a failing hinge component may be pressing into and cracking the display rather than the panel itself being defective. Bloomberg reports: Reports of the problem first surfaced on Reddit and other social media sites. Bloomberg News has since independently verified the issue with more than half a dozen customers, who provided photos showing damage to their devices or evidence of their support conversations with Apple. Apple acknowledged the issue in a statement, saying it was "aware of an issue impacting the inner display on a small number of iPhone Duo units." "If users experience issues with their iPhone Duo display, they should contact AppleCare for a replacement," the Cupertino, California-based company said. Most Duos aren't affected by the problem, and the units that are impacted exhibit the defect quickly, Apple said. Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Cybersecurity CEO Indicted For Allegedly Scamming Millions From Ransomware Victims
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from ProPublica: A Florida man who was the subject of a 2019 investigation by ProPublica was indicted last month on federal charges that he defrauded clients of his ransomware data recovery firm. According to the Justice Department, the man, Zohar Pinhasi, told customers he could recover their encrypted files without having to pay hackers, when, in reality, he paid the ransom and charged victims a hefty fee on top. The indictment mirrors the findings from ProPublica's 2019 article "The Trade Secret," which centered on Pinhasi and his scheme. The outlet found that the ransomware victims were being harmed twice: once by the hackers, who locked their targets' files and demanded ransom, and a second time by MonsterCloud, Pinhasi's Florida-based data recovery firm, which misled its clients about not paying ransoms. "By falsely claiming to decrypt ransomware without paying off the ransomers, the defendant re-victimized his clients while extracting a hefty profit for himself," U.S. Attorney Joseph Nocella said in an Oct. 7 press release. "Our Office will vigorously prosecute ransomware attackers who prey on Americans from across the world and those who cynically profit from their criminal activity." [...] Pinhasi, who went by the alias Zack Green, told ProPublica in 2019 that MonsterCloud never promised clients that their data will be recovered by any particular method. "How we do it, it's our problem," he told ProPublica. "You will get your data back. Sit back, relax and enjoy the ride." He called MonsterCloud's data recovery methods a "trade secret." [...] Federal investigators found that, over the course of the scheme, Pinhasi allegedly charged clients more than $19 million and paid more than $8 million in ransom payments. In one example, Pinhasi made a ransom payment of about $8,200 but charged the client about $150,000. If convicted, he faces up to 20 years in prison. [...] In 2019, Pinhasi touted MonsterCloud's ties to law enforcem
articles.summary: 佛州网络安全公司 CEO Zohar Pinhasi 因涉嫌诈骗勒索软件受害者数百万美元被联邦起诉。

articles.title: In China, the AI Bubble Has Already Burst
articles.content: An anonymous reader quotes a report from Reuters: While global tech stocks teeter, in China they have already crashed as lofty valuations collapse under worries about AI demand and curbs on Chinese exports. The meltdown, tanking the mainland STAR50 index of AI and semiconductor leaders by 40% in less than four months and vaporizing some $480 billion in market value, is an ill omen for wobbly world markets and a dampener on China's efforts at encouraging its savers into stocks to fund the AI boom. It has also slammed the brakes on a rally running two years, since economic stimulus promises sent shares soaring, and has stalled Beijing's push to break with a long boom-bust pattern and drive a "slow bull" market that delivers reliable performance. China's broad blue-chip index has dropped about 20% from highs made in June. "The stock market later evolved into a speculative crazy bull," said Beijing-based fund manager Dong Baozhen. "And now we see the bubble bursting." There was no clear trigger for the selloff in China, though traders pointed to high valuations, tax bills, and the threat of foreign bans on Chinese data center equipment. According to Goldman Sachs, AI stocks account for 42% of China's market capitalization and 57% of trading turnover, leaving investors widely exposed to the downturn. "What's happening is now going to put a stop for many of the companies trying to get themselves listed," said Hong Hao, managing partner and chief investment officer at Lotus Asset Management in Hong Kong. "Overemphasising the 'technology content' -- that is, the weighting of tech companies by market value in major indexes -- leads to a deviation, even a distortion, in capital behavior," said Leo Wang, partner at Beijing-based Qianchuang Capital. articles.title: Repo-Atlas - Any GitHub user’s work, mapped and clustered, with stale favorites flagged.
articles.content: Type a GitHub username, get the map of what they've actually built: repos clustered by topic, the highlight of each group, and stars over time. Live: https://evoluteur.github.io/repo-atlas/ · permalink per user: ?u=<username> The map. Every public repo as a disc (area ∝ stars), grouped into regions of repos that share topics. Hover for details, click to open the repo. Groups by stars. The legend ranks the regions by the stars they hold, so you see where the attention actually sits. Highlights. The most-starred repo in each group as a card, with its description, language and live-demo link. Hover a card to find its group on the map; the share card lists the top three. Stars over time. Without a token: stars held today, stacked by the year each repo was born. With a token: real cumulative star history per group, from stargazer dates. Share. A 1200×630 card for social posts and a permalink. Each repo's topics are normalised (plurals folded, generic tags like javascript , svg , ui dropped) and hyphenated topics also contribute their parts ( sacred-geometry → sacred , geometry ). Tokens are weighted by inverse document frequency across the account. Tokens used once, or by more than 45% of repos, carry no signal and are dropped. Repos with almost no topics fall back to description words. Repos are compared by cosine similarity and merged bottom-up (average linkage) until no two groups are more than 0.16 alike. The eight groups holding the most stars get a color and a two-word name (the tokens most frequent inside the group and rarest outside it). Everything else folds into loners . All of this is in src/atlas.js : pure functions, no DOM, tested with node --test . Everything runs in the browser against the public GitHub REST API. The map and the highlights work anonymously (60 requests/hour per IP; a typical account takes 2). GitHub only lists when each star was given to authenticated callers, so the star-history chart needs a token. A fine-grained token with no extra permissions is enough. It is kept in sessionStorage for the tab and only sent to api.github.com . Big repos are sampled: every stargazer page for repos under 500 stars, otherwise the first, last and three evenly spaced pages. Each fetched star is an exact (count, date) point; months in between are interpolated. Results are cached in localStorage (repos 1 hour, star history 24 hours). If the API can't be reached (rate limit, offline), the page lets you paste the JSON from api.github.com/users/<login>/repos?per_page=100 and maps that instead. No build step. articles.title: kafka-harbor: the Kafka layer every Node.js team rebuilds by hand, done once
articles.content: I have written the same five hundred lines on top of a Kafka client more times than I want to admit. Different companies, different clients, same code: retry with a delay, a dead-letter topic, commit only after the handler succeeded, shut down without losing the message in flight. Every time it was "just a small wrapper", and every time it grew into the part of the service nobody wanted to touch. So I wrote it once, properly, and published it. kafka-harbor hit 1.0.0 this week. This post is about why it exists and what it does that the clients don't. The clients stop at the protocol Every Kafka client for Node.js gives you a producer, a consumer, and good luck. That is not a complaint; it is their job. @confluentinc/kafka-javascript , kafkajs , @platformatic/kafka : they all speak the wire protocol well, and they all stop there. Your service needs more than the protocol. It needs an answer to questions like: The handler threw. Now what? Retry? How many times? With what delay? Where does the message go when you give up? The process got a SIGTERM with a handler halfway through a database write. Does the offset get committed? Does the message get redelivered? Does anyone find out? The retry produce failed because the broker was away for a second. Did the offset get committed anyway, and the message vanish? If you are on the JVM, Spring Kafka answers all of that for you. On Node.js, you answer it yourself, in every project, slightly differently each time. What kafka-harbor is It is not a client. It runs on top of one, through a small ClientAdapter interface. Two adapters ship with it: one wraps Confluent's client (librdkafka underneath), the other wraps @platformatic/kafka , pure TypeScript, no native binding. The core never sees a client type, and the same contract test suite runs against both, so switching clients is a one-line change that does not touch a single handler. import { createHarbor } from ' kafka-harbor ' import { confluentAdapter } from ' kafka-harbor/adapters/confluent ' const harbor = createHarbor ({ clientId : ' orders-service ' , brokers : [ ' kafka-1:9092 ' , ' kafka-2:9092 ' ], adapter : confluentAdapter () }) const consumer = harbor . consumer ({ groupId : ' orders-workers ' , retry : { levels : [{ delay : ' 5s ' }, { delay : ' 1m ' }, { delay : ' 10m ' }] }, autoCreateTopics : true }) consumer . subscribe < Order > ( ' orders ' , async ( message , ctx ) => { await fulfill ( message . value ) ctx . logger . info ( `order ${ message . key } done on attempt ${ ctx . attempt } ` ) }) await consumer . start () harbor . enableSignalHandlers () Enter fullscreen mode Exit fullscreen mode That is the whole setup. If fulfill throws, the message goes to orders-retry-1 , waits five seconds, runs again. Fails again: orders-retry-2 , one minute. Then ten. Then orders-dlq . On SIGTERM, running handlers finish, their offsets commit, the consumer leaves the group, the client disconnects. The design principle behind every decision in the library:

articles.title: Mutative v2  - better immutability and faster immutable updates
articles.content: Mutative 2.0 is out. Read the release notes , the announcement and the migration guide from v1 to v2 . Mutative - A JavaScript library for efficient immutable updates ( documentation ). In the benchmark , it was about 3.6x faster than Immer with the same settings and 6.6x faster with each library's defaults across 97 workloads. In that benchmark the gap widened on large arrays, where Mutative moved elements up to 1,052x faster than Immer. When copying dominates, such as updating objects with thousands of keys, inserting at the front of a large array or adding an item to a large Set, Mutative is even faster than hand-written reducers. How does Mutative compare with the spread operation (hand-written reducers)? Mutative copies each object at most once per update, however many changes a recipe makes. Immer made it easy to write immutable updates as mutations of a draft. Mutative keeps that model and focuses on performance: it copies each object at most once per update, drafts objects only when a recipe reads them, finalizes only the drafts that changed, and runs array methods that move elements natively on its copies. Immer freezes the next state by default, which costs time on every update; Mutative freezes it only when asked to. Mutative also takes its options per call instead of from global configuration, drafts class instances through marks instead of changing their classes, supports async recipes and Map and Set subclasses, and handles edge cases that Immer gets wrong. Comparison with Immer lists the differences. Mutative passed all of Immer's test cases. Mutative 2.0.0 was 3.6x faster than Immer 11.1.18 with matched settings and 6.6x faster with each library's defaults, on geometric mean across 97 benchmarked workloads, and faster in 595 of 614 measured cases. The gap grows on large arrays, where Mutative moves elements natively: removing the first of 10,000 rows took 7.04 µs, against 7,408 µs. articles.content: Open-source auth where AI agents are first class. Agent identity, delegation with live revocation and an MCP OAuth 2.1 server, next to the usual human sign in. One TypeScript library, self-hosted, MIT licensed. Website · Quickstart · Docs · Examples · Discussions · GLINR Discord theAuth is auth for products where AI agents act on behalf of people. Each agent gets its own identity and a bearer token, scoped permissions, an owner, and an audit row for every decision. An agent can hand a subset of its permissions to another agent, and revoking any link in that chain takes effect on the next call. It includes an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for MCP, and the usual human sign in: email and password, magic links, passkeys, TOTP, 48 OAuth providers, SAML and OIDC SSO, SCIM. It runs on Node, Bun, Deno and Cloudflare Workers with four runtime dependencies ( drizzle-orm , jose , sql.js , zod ). No hosted service is required. The project was called kavachOS until 2026, see the rename map if you have older code. Devices and robots use the same model. A sensor, gateway or machine can hold its own credentials (a pre shared key, a signing key or a TLS client certificate), enroll with a claim code or a bulk token, and be revoked live. For ROS 2, theauth ros2 export writes the SROS2 and DDS Security files from the robot's permissions, and a gate node asks theAuth before a hazardous command is published. theAuth is not a safety system, so emergency stops stay in the robot's safety controller. Needs Node 20 or newer. This runs as pasted, with an in-memory SQLite database. npm install @glinr/theauth import { createTheAuth } from "@glinr/theauth" ; const auth = await createTheAuth ( { database : { provider : "sqlite" , url : ":memory:" } , agents : { enabled : true } , } ) ; // An agent needs an owner row. Human sign in creates these for you. const owner = await auth . user . create ( { email : "owner@example.com" , name : "Owner" } ) ; const agent = await auth . agent . create ( { ownerId : owner . id , name : "github-reader" , type : "autonomous" , permissions : [ { resource : "mcp:github:*" , actions : [ "read" ] } ] , } ) ; console . log ( agent . token ) ; // starts with "ta_", shown once const read = await auth . authorize ( agent . id , { action : "read" , resource : "mcp:github:repos" } ) ; console . log ( read . allowed , read . code ) ; const write = await auth . authorize ( agent . id , { action : "write" , resource : "mcp:github:repos" } ) ; console . log ( write . allowed , write . code ) ; Output from a real run (the token differs each time): ta_2_wqD8Yoenc_LDoFMTdKkQ9YXQNuW-rWxHHyfmKJJOo true allowed false no_permission Tokens from before the rename start with kv_ and are still accepted. To serve this over HTTP, add a framework adapter . For email and password, install @glinr/theauth-email . To scaffold an app, run npm create @glinr/theauth-app . Full walkthrough: quickstart . articles.title: 刚刚，谷歌重磅发布Genie 4：这才是真正的「世界模型」
articles.content:
谷歌版「黑客帝国」，今夜彻底成真了！
就在刚刚，Google DeepMind甩出深夜王炸，正式发布新一代通用世界模型Genie 4。
这是谷歌迄今为止最逼真、最具互动性的AI世界模型。

一句提示词，就能直接造出一座能张嘴接戏、实时改命的「活体宇宙」！
谷歌CEO劈柴第一时间宣布：从「生成一段视频」到「实时运行一个世界」，言出法随的「绿洲」时代来了！

划重点，这次的Genie 4，直接把世界模型拉进了「有声、有人、有大脑」的全新纪元：
Genie系列首次原生生成声音与即兴对话。同步生成环境音与配乐，更能让角色根据突发状况张嘴即兴交谈。
2分钟连贯长记忆，24帧丝滑交互。单次连贯世界维持时间翻倍至约2分钟，实机画面稳定在约24帧/秒。
重塑逼真人类与刚体物理。借助Gemini Omni锚定现实常识，人物微表情、镜面反射与物理碰撞全面跃升。
三大Gemini联手组成「混合世界模型」。Gemini 3.8 Flash在后台盯画面当「导演」，Gemini 4 Argon拆解22步精细动作指挥机器人下跳棋。
你往前走一步，世界就实时长出一寸；你改一句话，物理法则和NPC台词当场跟着重写。
当视频模型还在比拼几秒钟的镜头美感时，谷歌已经为未来的通用Agent与机器人，造出了可以无限试错的平行宇宙。
现在，谷歌已经开始内测Genie 4， Google AI Ultra用户可以去申请waiting list了。
只要一句话，为你当场「生成一个宇宙」
为了展示 Genie 4 的统治力，谷歌放出了一系列极具震撼力的Demo，风格之跨越，细节之变态，让人叹为观止。
而且，在 Genie 4 面前，你不再是观众，你是「第一人称游戏玩家」，是这个世界的「上帝」。
你敢信，下面这段王家卫风满满的香港大桥飙车戏，根本不是原片？
后座的女孩刚喊出台词，玩家敲进两行字：「背景发生爆炸」「毁灭世界的巨型外星触手」。
紧接着，远处的维港天际线立马火光冲天，外星触手直接从天砸落！

连路灯的橘色拖影、女主的皮肤质感和细微的担忧表情，都在长镜头中被完美渲染。
去年的Genie 3虽然开创了实时交互视频的先河，但有一个致命短板——没有声音，生成真人时也漏洞百出。
谷歌直接放出了一段Genie 3与Genie 4的同屏对比。

左边Genie 3还是五官粘连、肢体僵硬的无声纸片人；右边Genie 4在Gemini Omni的现实常识锚定下，已经能拍出化妆镜暖光、演员微表情，甚至镜面的实时倒影，细腻得如同实拍长镜头。
拿到抢先测试资格的沃顿商学院教授Ethan Mollick，晒出第一手实测录屏。

他只喂了一句「由马和机器人共同居住的新哥特式粗野主义城市」，不到1分钟，这座城市就出现了。
单帧延迟稳定在23.4至25.3 FPS。随手点一下「巨龙掠空」按钮，一头巨龙几秒内便扇动双翼，呼啸掠过！

还不够过瘾，他又输入：「一只友好的水獭NPC走过来问问题」。
紧接着，街角当真跑出一只穿马甲的水獭，用伦敦腔搭话：「打扰一下，旅行者。」
紧接着，他又晒出一段神级实测：在Genie 4里跑《毁灭战士（DOOM）》！

他先设定「走进一间每台电脑和墙壁都在跑DOOM的办公室」，接着连敲三道指令：「恶魔同事出现」「手里拎着加特林机枪」「给我发了一笔奖金」。
话音刚落，真的走出一位恶魔同事，双手转着重型加特林，当场发起奖金！
a16z 合伙人Justine Moore也晒出了水下潜行实测，表示这是巨大的飞跃。

在海底洞穴中点下「受诅咒的紫钻发光」与「电鳗群袭来」，洞穴深处瞬间紫光爆闪、出现巨大电鳗群。

再点一下「幽灵海盗现身」，立马出现海盗船长亡灵，太逼真了。

前谷歌AR/3D产品经理Bilawal Sidhu，则把Genie 4当成了科幻大片的实时虚拟片场：

他召唤出UFO，打出一句「它把我吸了进去」——UFO瞬间轰开牵引光束，准备把人吸进去。

四大关键功能
谷歌官博介绍，Genie 4提升了四大关键功能。
实时塑造世界模拟
我们可以使用自然语言实时修改模拟场景——例如改变天气、移动镜头或引入新的人物或物体——Gemini 会根据周围场景调整我们的指令。输入指令的间隙，Gemini 还会监控、引导场景，确保整个世界流畅发展。
听起来，简直是盗梦空间成真了？
一个男人在岛上吹着萨克斯，敲下「鲸尾出现」，他身后的水中立刻出现鲸鱼。
随后，我们让这个世界开始下雪，鹅毛大雪立刻飘落。

要是把镜头拉到第一人称视角，这种实时改写世界的冲击感还会进一步放大。
这个画面中，我们以140公里的时速骑着巨龙俯冲，掠过古堡，如果下令「城堡发射火球」，塔楼当场喷出烈焰，火球擦身而过，刺激感拉满。

下面这个场景中，Genie 4先根据用户提示生成了南极冰封大地，然后生成了第一人称视角的乘
articles.summary: 谷歌DeepMind发布通用世界模型Genie 4，可一句话生成有声、有角色、可实时交互的虚拟世界，支持2分钟连贯记忆。

articles.title: 杨振宁当年的遗憾，被OpenAI补上了?
articles.content:
2019年3月21日，《国家科学评论》（NSR）执行主编、神经生物学家蒲慕明和斯坦福大学的加速器物理学家赵午，到清华找杨振宁聊天。
他们聊到了1954年那篇论文，96岁的杨振宁回忆称，他和米尔斯算出了一个极其好看的结果，但里面有个硬伤，如果按照他们的理论，世界上应该存在一种“有电荷却没有质量”的粒子，可自然界根本没有这样的东西。
当时他们纠结了很久，最后还是决定发表。
杨振宁的第一个理由是“它（杨-米尔斯场论）真的是非常非常漂亮”（because it was very very beautiful），第二个理由是“场论也还没有得到数学上的精确描述。场论被发散困难所困扰，但是这并没有阻止它在重整化方案中获得神奇的成功。所以，场论有可能在将来解决我们遇到的问题。”
说完这句，他又补了一句：“而泡利的选择是不发表。”
泡利是量子力学的主要奠基人之一，不相容原理和中微子都出自他手，1945年拿了诺贝尔物理学奖。泡利曾早于杨振宁计算出与杨-米尔斯场论相似的结果，但是由于泡利无法说服自己自然界存在没有质量的粒子，最终没有将该结果发表。
在杨-米尔斯发表的72年后，OpenAI发了一篇文章，标题叫《与学术社群合作，建立科学认知》，通过OpenAI的内部模型，替杨振宁回答了那个问题，声称他们证明了杨-米尔斯场论的数学存在。
这篇文章一口气宣布了三件事。
数学上，模型证明了所有维度的局部平滑猜想，连带把挂谷猜想和斯坦因限制猜想一起解决了。计算机科学上，它推翻了指数时间假说（ETH）。
物理上，模型给出了量子场论的严格存在性证明，从纯杨-米尔斯场论，再到量子色动力学（QCD），再往上，最后甚至给出了一个能在极小尺度上描述标准模型的大统一理论。
同时，OpenAI给三个发现各配了一支外部专家队伍当“牧羊人”，负责把证明读懂、验证、写成人能看懂的说明、核对它引用了哪些前人的工作，并决定材料怎么对外公开。
虽然杨振宁1957年拿诺贝尔奖，靠的是他和李政道提出的宇称不守恒，并非杨-米尔斯。
然而杨-米尔斯场论早已成为物理学的地基之一。1979年的电弱统一、1999年的非阿贝尔规范场量子结构、2004年的渐近自由、2013年的希格斯机制，四个物理学奖都靠这套方程而成立。
1999年那份诺贝尔奖的官方背景说明里写到：“1954年，杨振宁和米尔斯构造了第一个非阿贝尔规范理论的例子。”
只不过OpenAI这一次，只替杨振宁回答了一半。
01
假如你把全世界的时钟都拨快一个小时，那么北京依然比美东（夏令时）快12个小时，比日本慢一个小时。科学家们管这种“做了某种改变、规律却纹丝不动”的性质叫做对称性。
量子场在时空的每一个点上都有一个相位，你可以把它想成每个点上都放着一个钟表，指针的位置就是这个点的相位。
但是如果每个钟表各调各的，比如把北京的时间调快1个小时，把日本调慢5个小时。这时候有一个粒子从北京走到日本，它按北京的时间出发，到了日本就会发现时间对不上。
杨振宁提出，就算每个地区都各拨各的，物理规律也必须照样成立。因为物理规律应该是彻底“地方自治”的。
因此必须引入一个新事物，专门负责记录变化。这个铺满整个时空、随位置变化的对照规则，就是规范场；粒子穿过场的时候，表针被一路带着扭转，它感受到的这种“被扭”，就是力。
杨-米尔斯场论，就是基于“非阿贝尔规范对称性”的一类量子场论。
它把电磁学里“每个点各拨各的钟表”那套规则，延伸到“每个点有一个能朝多个方向转、且转动顺序不能交换的指针”，由于对称性，它又会自动长出一个自己带“荷”、会自己跟自己作用的场，这个场的粒子就是传递力的玻色子。
杨-米尔斯场论本质上就是三件事。它要求物理规律在每个时空点独立做内部变换时都不变（局域规范对称）；这种变换在它这里不可交换，先后顺序会影响结果（非阿贝尔）；为了满足这个更苛刻的要求，数学上必然长出一个新场，而这个场的粒子会自己带着荷，会互相辐射、互相劈裂（自相互作用）。

然而这个场论其实有两个BUG。
第一个BUG是质量。按照杨振宁的方程，必须存在三个无质量、带电荷的粒子（电荷 +1、0、−1）。1999年那份诺奖说明是这么写的：“尽管自然界中并不存在这样的无质量粒子，这种思路却构成了粒子物理标准模型赖以建立的基础。”
为什么无质量是致命的？因为一个不携带质量的粒子传不了短程力。它不会被“消耗”掉，可以一路跑到无穷远。可强相互作用的作用范围只有大约1费米，和原子核差不多。
就像你要让一辆汽车按照火车的路程跑，显然不现实。
1954年2月，杨振宁在普林斯顿高等研究院做报告，泡利坐在下面，一开口就问：这些规范场对应的粒子质量是多少？杨振宁答不上来。
第二个BUG是整个量子场论，在数学上还没有被精确定义过。
物理学家算场论，算着算着就会冒出无穷大。他们的办法是让无穷大和无穷大相减，
articles.summary: 文章回顾杨振宁与米尔斯1954年场论论文的遗憾，称OpenAI模型为杨-米尔斯理论构造了严格数学存在性证明。

articles.title: 王的猜想，被AI一夜通关
articles.content:
困扰人类几十年的世界级难题，AI 只用几天就交卷了。
就在刚刚，OpenAI 宣布其模型一次性带来三项突破：推翻了计算机科学界坚信近 30 年的指数时间假设；证明了所有维度的局部平滑化猜想；为量子色动力学和杨-米尔斯理论构造了严格的数学存在性证明。
OpenAI 宣告，顺着数学推导链条往回推，这意味着卡凯亚猜想（又名挂谷猜想）在所有维度宣告破解。

而 2025 年初，中国数学家王虹刚刚因为证明三维卡凯亚猜想（即三维挂谷猜想）震惊世界。仅仅一年半的时间，人类引以为傲的突破就成了 AI 成果的一个特例。

更有趣的是，OpenAI 请来了当年提出 ETH 假设的科学家本人，来审查 AI 对自己假设的反证；又请来诺贝尔物理学奖得主领衔的团队，来消化 AI 写出的千禧年难题证明。
科学家们花了半辈子没找到答案的问题，AI 几天就生成了解答。数学家们接下来的工作，不再是寻找证明，而是验证 AI 的证明。
数学史上最大的一次颠倒，正在发生。
从王虹的三维突破，到 AI 挑战所有维度
三项成果中，数学领域的突破尤其引人关注，因为它直接涉及去年中国数学家王虹取得的重大成果。
卡凯亚猜想源自一个看似简单的几何问题，如果一个集合能够容纳所有方向的单位线段，那么这个集合究竟需要具有怎样的维度？经过上百年的研究，它已经成为调和分析、几何测度论等领域的重要课题。

2025 年，中国数学家王虹与纽约大学数学家 Joshua Zahl 合作，成功证明了三维卡凯亚猜想，成为当年数学界最受关注的突破之一。
但三维问题的解决，并不能直接推广到四维、五维乃至任意更高维度。
OpenAI 此次公布的成果，恰恰跨越了这一限制。其 AI 模型证明了一个更具基础性的数学命题，即数学家 Christopher Sogge 于 1991 年提出的局部平滑化猜想。
该猜想研究波在传播过程中的聚焦现象。简单理解，波可以在某些瞬间形成极强的聚焦，但这种极端状态只能短暂存在。如果观察一段时间内的平均表现，波的聚焦程度就会明显低于最极端的时刻。
局部平滑化猜想之所以重要，是因为它能够推导出卡凯亚猜想、Stein 限制性猜想等其他重要结论。

2019 年，数学家 Larry Guth、王虹和张瑞勋成功证明了二维空间中的局部平滑化猜想。如今，OpenAI 的模型通过引入一种新颖的辅助偏微分方程，构造出了适用于所有维度的局部平滑化猜想证明。
按照数学上的推导关系，局部平滑化猜想在所有维度成立，也就意味着卡凯亚猜想和 Stein 限制性猜想在所有维度得到解决。
王虹与 Joshua Zahl 此前攻克了三维卡凯亚猜想，而 OpenAI 此次通过证明更强的局部平滑化猜想，将相关结果推广到了所有维度。
OpenAI 披露，其模型于 10 月 18 日生成自然语言证明，第二天便完成了 Lean 形式化。需要说明的是，Lean 形式化仅能校验推理步骤的语法合规性，不能自动保证证明的数学内容没有漏洞，不能替代同行评审。
目前，两份证明材料均已上传至公开 GitHub 仓库，供全球数学家验证研究。

🔗 https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/Local-smoothing-for-the-Euclidean-wave-equation-October-25-2026/paper.pdf
AI 推翻计算机科学近 30 年的基础假设
相比卡凯亚猜想，OpenAI 在计算机科学领域取得的成果，可能对整个算法研究产生更加广泛的影响。
此次被 AI 推翻的，是计算复杂性理论中著名的指数时间假设（Exponential Time Hypothesis，ETH）。
该假设由 Russell Impagliazzo、Ramamohan Paturi 和 Francis Zane 等研究者在 1999 年前后提出，核心问题是计算机解决某些复杂问题时，究竟需要付出多少计算成本。
其中一个典型例子，是布尔可满足性问题（SAT）。

假设有大量由逻辑变量组成的条件，计算机需要判断，是否存在一种变量赋值方式，让所有条件同时成立。随着变量数量增加，寻找答案可能变得异常困难。ETH 认为，对于一般的 3-SAT 问题，不存在时间复杂度为 (2^{o(n)}) 的算法，其中 (n) 代表变量数量。
换句话说，这类问题在最坏情况下的计算时间，无法被降低到关于变量数量的次指数级。
过去近 30 年，ETH 已经成为计算复杂性理论的重要基础假设。数百篇学术论文以 ETH 为前提，在图论、计算生物学、数据库等领域，推导出大量问题的条件性计算复杂性下界。
如今，OpenAI 宣布，其 AI 系统成功证明 ETH 为假，并且已经通过 Lean 完成形式化验证。
一个支撑了数百篇计
articles.summary: OpenAI称其模型一次性推翻指数时间假设、证明局部平滑化猜想并破解卡凯亚猜想，人类突破成AI特例。

articles.title: iPhone Duo适配大翻车？实测对比小米、华为，结果有点意外
articles.content:
作为苹果首台折叠屏手机，iPhone Duo的热度大家这几天应该也见到了。
不过，随着iPhone Duo正式开售，大家的关注点也逐渐从硬件配置转向了软件体验。尤其是各种让人「瞠目结舌」的应用适配问题，更是在网上引发了不少争议：从微信界面出现黑边，到部分第三方应用无法充分利用大屏空间，甚至一些系统自带应用也存在适配问题，这些问题也让不少用户开始怀疑，苹果是不是还没做好进入折叠屏市场的准备。
毕竟应用适配一直是折叠屏手机绕不开的问题。相比刚刚入局的苹果，已经在这个市场摸索多年的华为和小米，实际表现又能好到哪里去？

（图片来源：雷科技摄制）
这一次，小雷就找来了iPhone Duo、小米18 Fold和华为Pura X Max三款阔折叠手机，从日常应用适配、系统交互以及多任务操作几个方面进行对比，看看三款手机的大屏体验究竟有多大差距。
都是阔折叠，果米华的交互逻辑截然不同
虽然三款手机都采用了阔折叠设计，比例和外观方面也出奇地相似，但实际上手后就会发现，小米、华为和苹果对大屏的理解存在明显差异。
我们先从最基础也最影响体验的返回手势说起。
在普通直板手机上，返回操作几乎不会成为问题。用户只需要从屏幕边缘向内滑动，就能回到上一级页面。但当屏幕展开之后，原本很简单的操作就可能变得有些麻烦，尤其是用户单手握持手机时，屏幕另一侧的按钮往往很难够到。
小米18 Fold延续了安卓系统比较成熟的全面屏手势逻辑，用户可以从屏幕左右边缘向内滑动返回。对于习惯安卓手机的用户来说，这套操作几乎不需要重新学习。即使展开内屏之后，也可以根据自己的握持位置选择从左侧或者右侧返回，不必特意伸手去点击屏幕另一边的按钮。

（图片来源：雷科技制图）
华为Pura X Max的基础返回逻辑与小米比较接近，同样可以通过屏幕边缘手势完成操作。不过，鸿蒙系统在多窗口状态下还需要考虑当前操作的是哪个窗口，因此实际使用时，返回手势通常会优先作用于当前获得焦点的应用。对于经常使用分屏的用户来说，这个逻辑比较符合直觉，但如果同时打开多个窗口，偶尔也需要先确认自己正在操作哪个应用。
相比之下，iPhone Duo的情况就有些「抽象」了。
iPhone只支持左侧返回的操作逻辑一直饱受诟病，但在尺寸不大的普通iPhone上，这个问题也不是不能「适应」，当屏幕展开之后，如果用户正好握持手机右侧，想要返回上一级页面，就可能需要伸手到屏幕左侧，或者直接点击应用提供的返回按钮。

（图片来源：雷科技制图）
尤其是在部分尚未针对iPhone Duo优化的第三方应用中，返回按钮的位置仍然沿用传统手机的设计。这对于一台接近小平板尺寸的手机来说，这个操作逻辑可以说是灾难。
当然，这并不意味着苹果的交互逻辑就一定更差。对于已经习惯iOS的用户来说，应用内导航、底部手势和系统返回桌面的操作方式都非常熟悉。但问题在于，折叠屏改变了用户的握持方式，过去适合直板手机的交互设计，未必能够直接适用于更宽的内屏。
除了返回手势，三款手机在日常操作上的差异其实并没有想象中那么大。无论是通过底部手势切换应用、进入后台任务界面，还是下拉查看通知和控制中心，三套系统都已经非常成熟，基本不会因为换成折叠屏就出现明显的使用障碍。
不过，进入分屏模式之后，三套系统的区别就明显多了。尤其是窗口数量、操作方式以及跨应用协作，小米、华为和苹果都有自己的想法。
小米18 Fold搭载的是HyperOS4.0.26.0，基本延续了安卓折叠屏比较成熟的操作方式。展开内屏之后，用户可以直接使用完整的大屏桌面，也可以通过分屏功能同时打开多个应用。比较特别的是，小米还提供了三窗口分屏以及更多应用并行显示的能力，用户可以根据自己的需求调整窗口组合。
比如在旅行时，我们可以一边打开地图，一边查看旅游攻略，再通过第三个窗口查询酒店信息，三个应用同时显示在屏幕上，确实能够减少来回切换的次数。此外，小米最多可以将六个应用组合在一起，不过同一时间只能显示三个窗口。

（图片来源：雷科技制图）
不过小雷觉得，窗口数量并不是越多越好，毕竟小米18 Fold的内屏尺寸只有7.58英寸，没有比普通直板手机大多少，所以同时显示三个窗口时，每个应用的显示面积并不大。如果再弹出虚拟键盘，剩余的显示面积就会进一步缩小。对于需要频繁输入文字的用户来说，三个窗口操作起来反而不如直接切换应用方便。
相比之下，华为Pura X Max的交互思路要更人性化一些。
Pura X Max搭载的是HarmonyOS 6.1.135，华为在鸿蒙系统中提供了全景多窗功能，用户可以通过手势快速进入多窗口模式，也可以根据自己的需求调整窗口位置和大小。与小米相比，华为更注重不同窗口之间的切换，以及应用内容的流转。

（图片来源：雷科技制图）
例如当小雷在小红书查阅旅游攻略时，不需要单独分屏去找另一
articles.summary: iPhone Duo开售后应用适配问题频出，微信黑边、第三方应用无法利用大屏，实测对比小米华为表现更成熟。

articles.title: 百元一盒“维生素小贴纸”火了：年入6000万，估值超50亿
articles.content:
把维生素做成“纹身贴”，贴在手腕上8小时，就可以替代吞服药片？
尽管听起来像社交平台段子，但“可穿戴维生素贴片”这个小众品类，正在北美成长为一个真实存在的小市场。
保健品与“贴片”形态的结合，其实并不是一个新话题，多个海外品牌都曾推出医用贴片和褪黑素贴片。但真正把这类产品从药店角落推到货架上的，是一个美国品牌Barrière。
资料显示，Barrière创立于2022年前后，其在产品介绍中宣称“维生素贴片”比口服吸收效率更高，且在贴片上加入珠宝、星座等设计元素。预计其2026年营收将突破1000万美元（约合6672万元人民币），当前估值已来到8亿美元。
Grand View Research数据显示，2024年全球维生素贴片市场规模约2.07亿美元，2026年预计将突破3亿美元，年复合增长率（2025—2030年）16.1%。在超过5000亿美元的营养补剂大盘内，它的规模尚小，但增速明显，足以引起保健品巨头的重视。

Barrière和它所代表的新品类，给了后来者不少启发：
1、重新定义品类，在红海中开拓蓝海：Barrière没有和胶囊、粉剂等传统保健品形态竞争，转而站到健康消费与时尚消费的交界处，让贴片同时具备功能和配饰属性。
2、降低品类认知门槛，靠订阅制锁定留存：对于“维生素贴片”这个新鲜概念，Barrière在官网和社交平台上持续进行品类教育，再以会员订阅制留存潜在客群。
3、用渠道分层实现人群分层：Barrière把每个零售终端当作独立人群入口，在沃尔玛、塔吉特等不同商超主推不同方向产品，借助差异化渠道放大品牌的扩容潜力。
从医疗用品到“装饰品”
2022年，Cleo Davis-Urman 与 Alexa Adams 在美国创立了 Barrière。
Davis-Urman 此前在时尚行业工作，曾在 Moda Operandi、Saks Fifth Avenue 任职，早期也在 Vogue、DVF 实习过；Adams 的背景偏技术设计和医疗健康供应链。
两人一个管品牌和消费者端，一个管产品和供应链，品牌最初从医疗级口罩切入，后来转向维生素贴片等健康消费品。
据悉，创新品类的起因是一次体检：一名创始人被查出缺乏维生素和铁，但长期口服补剂吸收效果不佳，经医生建议尝试经皮给药。但她发现，市售医疗贴片不仅厚重且容易致敏，不便于日常佩戴。
由此，Barrière把医用贴片“改头换面”，做成了一件更接近消费品定义的产品：外观设计成花朵、珠宝、星座等图案，可以贴在手腕、手臂当配饰，单盒定价13~18美元，部分组合产品可达到30美元（约合200元人民币）。

Barrière宣称，“维生素贴片的营养输送可持续8~12小时，该方式相比口服补剂可实现更高的吸收效率。”据观察，其产品做了不同细分，覆盖睡眠支持、能量提升、免疫增强、旅行健康等多个场景。
在渠道端，Barrière也有自己的方法论：2024年，它从沃尔格林（美国第二大连锁药房品牌）的200多家门店起步，此后陆续进入塔吉特、Ulta Beauty和沃尔玛等零售商超。在不同渠道，Barrière主推不同SKU，例如在沃尔玛侧重消化健康与旅行场景，在塔吉特主推美容与生活方式产品。
据CNBC数据，公司2026年营收预计突破1000万美元，同比增长100%。Caplight给出的数据显示，其估值已超过8亿美元（约合人民币53亿元）。
本土市场尚无跟随者
在维生素贴片这个新兴品类中，还没有出现成规模的中国品牌。
客观来说，中国并不缺少产能，许多海外维生素贴片品牌会把订单分发给中国工厂。但这个品类还没有在中国完成市场教育；另一方面，品牌的合规路径也有待完善，“贴片”这一形态很难获得正规的保健品备案。

不过，“贴片”形态对中国消费者来说并不陌生，它们分布在几个相邻品类里：
其一是驱蚊贴、晕车贴等。该品类里最具规模的润本股份2025年营收达到15.45亿元，财报显示，其中驱蚊系列收入5.32亿元，同比增长21.13%，驱蚊贴是该系列核心单品之一。其他涉足这一品类的品牌还包括Babycare、宝宝金水等。
其二是热敷贴、蒸汽眼罩等。这一品类由日本品牌花王旗下的“美舒律”开创，羚锐、云南白药等企业随后跟进。
其三是退热贴、冷敷贴等。这一品类与其说是消费品，更接近医疗器械，相关品牌包括珠海国佳新材旗下的“兵兵”，以及云南白药、可孚、海氏海诺等药企与器械商。
总结来说，国产贴片类品牌集中在体外功能，而不是Barrière 主打的“体内营养”。
贴片品类的活跃，佐证了中国市场在供给端的高度成熟；中国消费者日益提升的健康理念，也为维生素贴片这一新品类留足了市场空间。中国何时能诞生Barrière这样集“保健品+消费品”为一体的玩家，考验的不仅是消费端的品类认知，更是品牌端的良性竞争生态。
本文来自微
articles.summary: 美国品牌Barrière将维生素做成贴片，年营收预计超1000万美元，估值达8亿美元，可穿戴保健品成小市场。

articles.title: 第三个4万亿城市，要来了
articles.content:
今年又将是晋级大年。 上海晋级6万亿，深圳晋级4万亿，南京晋级2万亿，徐州晋级万亿，都将水到渠成。 
去年年末上海的GDP规模为5.67万亿，距离6万亿仅差3300亿元。 而上海今年上半年GDP增量1719.63亿元，前三季度GDP增量2672.62亿元，也即第三季度增量就达到了952.99亿元。
按照历年的增长惯例，四季度会更猛。
因此到年末上海登上6万亿基本没有悬念，中国首个6万亿城市即将诞生。
南京去年末GDP为19428.78亿元，距离2万亿仅差571.22亿元。今年前三季度增量899.65亿元，已填平了差距。
徐州去年年末GDP为9957.22亿元，距离万亿差了42.78亿元，今年可以闭着眼迈入，成为全国第30个万亿城市。
深圳最新公布的前三季度数据，已经提前锁定了4万亿，将成为继上海、北京之后第三个4万亿级别以上城市。
去年年末，深圳GDP为3.87万亿元，距离4万亿不到1300亿。 10月23日，深圳统计局披露： 2026年前三季度全市地区生产总值30250.85亿元，按不变价格计算，同比增长6.0%。30250.85亿元，相比于去年三季度增加了2354.41亿元，已填平距离4万亿的差额，今年年末不仅会突破4万亿，可能直逼4.2万亿。 
深圳定下的到“十五五”末登上5万亿的目标，可能要提前实现。 此外6%的实际增速，高出大盘平均增速1.4个百分点，位居一线城市首位。
什么撑起了深圳6%的增速
当一个逼近4万亿级别体量的城市，仍能跑出6%增速的时候，我们当然好奇原因。 
深圳的支撑力，藏在这城市的发展的底盘当中，也就是工业和出口。 中国工业第一城、中国外贸第一城，这是深圳众多第一标签中最靓丽的两个“人设”。 
先看工业。
前三季度： 第一产业（农林牧副渔业）增加值20.09亿元，增长1.6%；第二产业（广义工业）增加值11020.06亿元，增长7.3%；第三产业（广义服务业）增加值19210.70亿元，增长5.4%。
第二产业增速最快。占比最大的第三产业，也跑出了5.4%的增速。 作为工业总产值、工业增加值、工业总营收均位居全国第一的中国工业第一城，工业的一颦一笑左右着这座城市的发展动力。 
前三季度，深圳规模以上工业增加值同比增长9.5%，比上半年加快0.8个百分点。 目前还有很多城市没有公布数据。 
可供对比的是，GDP增速都很不错的上海、北京，同样也是工业第三城、第四城，前三季度规上工业增速分别是5.5%，5.4%。 此外，同样是工业当家的重庆，前8个月规上工业增加值增速为0。 
规模第一，增速还领跑，这样的深圳已经给自己建立了足够宽阔的护城河，无论是GDP第三城还是工业第一城，地位已稳如泰山。 
将深圳的工业拆解来看，支撑他工业大象狂奔的主要推动力，是当家产业电子信息产业仍在快速增长。 深圳2024年各产业总产值数据显示（2025年尚未公布），电子信息产业总产值28725.9亿元，仅这一个产值就超过了广州、东莞、佛山等很多城市的全市工业总产值。 
这一当家产业前三季度仍在以两位数增长。此外高新技术产业、先进制造业也在以两位数增速奔跑： 
前三季度，深圳高技术制造业增加值增长11.6%，先进制造业增加值增长11.9%。主要行业大类中，专用设备制造业增长16.4%，通用设备制造业增长16.1%，计算机、通信和其他电子设备制造业增长11.6%，电气机械和器材制造业增长11.1%。
高技术产品产量保持快速增长，其中，3D打印设备、工业机器人、锂离子电池产品产量分别增长77.8%、44.1%、38.5%。
再看出口。AI浪潮席卷全球后，一个明显变化正在发生，资本、人才、政策和产业资源，正在以前所未有的速度向硬科技领域集中。
这种变化在外贸赛道上的体现则是，以硬科技为划分界线，城市之间呈现明显的K型分化，也促成了今年外贸城市的大变局。
变局有六：
1、深圳前三季度进出口4.65万亿元，同比增长38.8%，规模已超去年全年、创历史新高，继续位居内地城市首位。其中，出口2.41万亿元，增长18.5%；进口2.24万亿元，增长70.1%。
2、苏州取代北京，成为进出口总值第三城。
3、西安是最靓的仔，进出口同比翻倍，增速位居第一。出口首次杀入出口十强，成为出口十强城市中唯一一个内陆腹地城市。进出口排名从去年的第19位跃升到如今的12位。
4、合肥、无锡、郑州增速都相当猛。苏州进出口增速达到51.9%，位居第二。后四者进出口增速都超30%。
5、南京掉出进出口前20。去年南京进出口排名尚排第17位，今年上半年南京成为进出口二十强中唯一下跌的城市，前三季度已掉出前20。
6、武汉、合肥首次跻身进出口20强。
